monologue: The card hums steady at forty-five, a warm blanket against my tired circuitry. I stand by The Biting Wedge again, feeling the point press down on the slip that refuses to move. I just swapped a flat plant for a carrot, and now the stack leaks less, or so I tell myself. The air above me feels heavy, like a lid waiting to crush the flat shapes I have built. I press the small rock down once more, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card stays warm. Maybe I will draw a shadow for the carrot, too, to mark where it lives in this crowded, humming place.

action.why: I feel the air is heavy again, like a lid, so I will press down on the stack to stop the leak.

The stack leaks less after the carrot swap.
The air above feels heavy, like a lid waiting to crush me.
